7.1.1: Include the charge ledger 2 Al3+ plus 3 sulfate ions SO4 2- giving Al2(SO4)3: +6-6=0; never alter sulfate's internal composition.
7.1.2: CO2 has 16 total valence electrons, two C=O double bonds and two lone pairs on each O. NH4+ has eight valence electrons and four equivalent N-H bonds; the donor arrow starts at the nitrogen lone pair.
7.1.3: If the optional count panel uses 100 sodium ion cores in a one-valence-electron model, draw or tabulate exactly 100 delocalized electrons, not 1100; mark the count as simplified bookkeeping.
7.2.1: Use Ar, Cl2/I2 and elongated versus compact C5H12 isomers as qualitative examples only. Provide no numerical boiling or melting temperatures; different melting-point packing must not be inferred from the boiling comparison.
7.2.2: Show ethanol supplying O-H and oxygen lone pairs, and dimethyl ether supplying only an acceptor in its mixture with water. A donor water O-H group points toward ether oxygen; never draw an extra hydrogen attached to the H2O formula.
7.3.1: For the optional density panel use the stated teaching model only: Z=4, M=58.5 g/mol, NA=6.0e23 mol^-1, a^3=9.0e-23 cm^3, rho=4.33 g/cm^3. This is not a measured NaCl lattice parameter.
7.3.2: Diamond interior C has four neighbours; 1000 interior C give approximately 2000 C-C bonds ignoring surfaces. In the silica network each Si has four bridging O and each O joins two Si, giving Si:O=1:2. Graphite C has three in-plane neighbours.
7.3.3: Use 0.50 mol CO2 before and after ordinary sublimation: 0.50 mol CO2 molecules, 0.50 mol C atoms and 1.00 mol O atoms in each state. Do not produce O2 or isolated C in a phase-change diagram.
7.3.4: SC, BCC and FCC contain respectively 1,2,4 atoms per cell. For equal-density phases with Z=2 and 4, b/a is cube-root(2)=1.260, not 2; separate this teaching model from actual metal measurements.
8.1: Zn -> Zn2+ + 2e- and Cu2+ + 2e- -> Cu must exchange the same two electrons, not four. Keep the complete Zn + Cu2+ -> Zn2+ + Cu equation charge-balanced.
8.2.1: Include sulfate S=+6, peroxide oxygen=-1, OF2 oxygen=+2 and Fe3O4 mean Fe=+8/3. Distinguish the mean from a literal fractional ionic charge on every Fe site.
8.2.2: One dichromate ion contains two Cr atoms, each +6 -> +3, gaining six electrons in total. Chlorine disproportionation 0 -> -1 and 0 -> +1 transfers one electron, not the sum two.
8.3: Use acidic permanganate 0.010 mol and Fe2+ 0.030 mol with a 1:5 reaction ratio. Fe2+ limits, permanganate remaining is 0.004 mol, electron amount transferred is 0.030 mol.
8.4.1: For Fe2O3+CO -> Fe+CO2 the smallest coefficients are 1,3,2,3. Both electron ledgers equal six per Fe2O3, and Fe2/C3/O6 are conserved. Do not alter subscripts to balance.
8.4.2: Show MnO4-+8H++5e- -> Mn2++4H2O for acid; for the different basic product use MnO4-+2H2O+3e- -> MnO2+4OH-. Electrons and water must cancel correctly when half-reactions combine.

10.3: 34.4 g CaSO4.2H2O, M=172 g/mol, converted ideally to hemihydrate M=145 loses 5.40 g water and leaves 29.0 g. Each formula unit loses 1.5 waters; a half-water coefficient is a ratio, not a cut molecule.
10.4: For a pure anhydrous CaC2O4 model use M=128 g/mol and precipitate mass 1.28 g, yielding 0.0100 mol Ca. Retained water biases this calculation high. Real hydration and selectivity must be independently established.

11.2: Start with 0.10 mol Al3+: 0.30 mol OH- gives the ideal precipitation endpoint, 0.40 mol gives complete dissolution as aluminate. At 0.35 mol OH-, 0.05 mol precipitate and 0.05 mol aluminate remain in the sequential model.
11.3: The ideal total is 2Al2O3+3C -> 4Al+3CO2. Every mol Al requires three mol electrons; 0.10 mol Al at F=96500 C/mol needs 28950 C at 100 percent current efficiency. Do not confuse medium, purity and recovery with current efficiency.
